spec_ambiguities_resolved: QEMU/Renode liveness: spec §12 X4/X5 exit checks say 'live XSDB session vs AMD QEMU'. No QEMU/Renode binary exists in this build environment. Resolution: adapters implement the full adapter interface + session semantics deterministically against a simulated PS, declare target_class=emulator in every record, and adapters/qemu_xsdb.py states plainly that NO live-transport binding exists in this build (no code binds one, no switch enables one). Governance outcomes (refusals, receipts, packs, verdicts) are identical by construction (adapter-parity test). Evidence class stays emulator; nothing is upgraded. Verity should note the live-process binding is unexercised in this environment.

persistent_capture (spec §6.1 supporting op): 'callable in-session' but explicitly NOT a surface tool (count must stay 22). Resolution: it is a bridge/engine operation (Bridge.call_session_op 'persistent_capture') inside tool 15's flow, reachable by the session host/tests, and absent from the MCP tools/list (it is even in the server FORBIDDEN_TOOL_NAMES set so a fuzzed call refuses as unknown-tool). T3 happy path (arm -> capture -> write) is fully test-exercised through it.

Pack 'evidence' section: §11.1 lists mandatory pack contents; Gate assertions (register_eq/memory_eq/boot_banner/power_state_eq) need evaluation data, so packs additionally carry an 'evidence' snapshot (console_text, registers, memory_hashes, power_state) captured at seal from the adapter/session. Mandatory §11.1 sections are all present; verify_pack requires every one of them and rejects stripped target_class (H-13).

Caps semantics: caps.max_read_bytes / max_write_bytes read as cumulative per-mandate ceilings alongside max_loads / max_power_cycles (§9.1 'caps'); boundary-exact refusal tested (§13.1). Recorded here so Verity benches the stated semantics.

Pack seal receipt: §11.2 says a seal receipt binds chain head + pack hash. Implemented as the pack-level 'seal' record (chain_head_sha256 + pack_sha256, bridge-signed) rather than an extra in-chain receipt, because the close op itself is receipted into the chain before sealing (session_close is in operations[] and receipts[] of its own pack).

Pre-session/boundary refusals (no session exists yet, or schema-denied params) receipt into the bridge refusal/op log chain (receipts.ReceiptChain 'bridge-ops') — §9.1's 'refusal record' — rather than a session pack.
session_open lease_expiry op code: an op on an EXPIRED session refuses LEASE_EXPIRED (H-5) rather than SESSION_FROZEN; SEALED/DROPPED sessions refuse SESSION_FROZEN.
